notes.title: Chrono Sword ver. 1.1.08 update – Sept. 25th, 2025
notes.content:
Hello, fellow time travelers.

Thank you all for supporting Chrono Sword during the wait.



Based on all of your feedback, we've made improvements in all sorts of areas. We hope that all of these new additions and improvements provide a satisfying, enjoyable gameplay experience.



Let us fill you in on the important changes coming in this update.



■ Gameplay system changes

- Level-up system simplified: Stats are now automatically increased on level up, and an additional 'Cyl Cryst' has been added as a reward.

- Skill tree system: Players may now use the Cyl Cryst they obtain to learn the skills they wish to use, improve stats, or unlock certain actions.

- Separating swords and shields: You can now freely swap out and combine various sword and shield combinations.

- Index NPCs: Increased accessibility by making various NPCs, like merchants, appear next to Indexes.

- Several other of the finer gameplay systems have been improved.



■ Improved combat and movement

- Improved running: Players can now make the character run by pushing the stick harder.

- Targeting system improved: The 'targeting vs. not targeting' method has now been changed to 'auto vs. manual targeting.'

- Parrying improvements: Now, after unlocking the appropriate skill, a successful Just Guard will trigger a parry.

- Just Avoid bonus: After unlocking the appropriate skill, a successful Just Avoid now recharges the 'Glyph of Healing.'

- Several other combat and movement systems have been improved for your experience.



■ Improved learning curve, difficulty, level design

- Added difficulty selections: You can now choose your difficulty on selecting a new game.

- Improved tutorials: The game now shows tutorial tips, and the levels are designed to allow players to adapt to the overall gameplay experience more easily.

- Level design improvements: Level configuration, enemy placement, and background design have all been improved to help players understand the overall flow of the game.

- Penalty for deaths adjusted: Only 50% of Cyl will be dropped on death, allowing for players to get back on track more easily.

Other learning curve, difficulty, and level design improvements have been made alongside this.



■ UI/UX Improvements

- In-game menu improved: Each menu has been improved to open immediately or quickly switch to another menu.

- Integrated inventory: Equipment, inventory, and stats have been combined to be seen on a single screen to help with visibility.

- Map system improved: The locations you've explored in the past and future are displayed in each zone for each timeline, increasing the fun of exploration.

- Improved language and resolution display: Fixed problems such as fonts displaying incorrectly for certain words, UI distorting at certain resolutions, and more.

Several other UI/UX improvements have been made.



■ Improved overall quality and production value

- Strengthened early-game experience: Improved early-game level design and production value to make a more immersive, exciting experience.

- Improved terrain height display: Improved background height delineation to make it easier to read and to improve immersion.

Improved object visibility: Changed folded ladder design, object placement, and more to help the overall level of understanding.

- Improved musical production value: Improved musical production value and added music to events, such as resting at Indexes, boss phase transitions, and more.

- Several other game quality/optimization issues have been improved upon.



■ Bug fixes

- Fixed issues where the game would not continue progressing as usual.

- Fixed issues where interactions in the past and future, such as door/object interactions, were not working as intended.

- Fixed issues where the targeting system would unlock from a target.

- Fixed combat-related bugs, such as when no knockback was applied when shot or the player couldn't pass through lasting spewed enemy projections.



Numerous other bugs have also been fixed.



We will continue striving to make a better gameplay experience into the future.

Thank you!

notes.title: Chrono Sword Update Notice - September 15th, 2025
notes.content:
Hello, fellow time travelers,



This is David from the Chrono Sword dev team, 21cDucks.



Chrono Sword will be getting its first update since entering early access. This first update will drop on Thursday, September 25th.



As I let you all know before, we've been thinking from multiple angles about how to improve the fun and overall experience of the game, and this update is sure to improve many parts of the gameplay experience and quality-of-life features that you've been suggesting.



I'll inform you all of the contents to be included in this update very soon!



As you play through Chrono Sword moving forward, feel free to share your thoughts on how to improve our game through the various channels available. Thank you, one and all!



Best wishes to everyone,

David

notes.title: Announcing the 2025 Steam Early Access update roadmap
notes.content:
Hello from the team at CFK.

We are excited to introduce today the 2025 Steam Early Access update roadmap for new pixel art souls-like action RPG 'Chrono Sword'.

'Chrono Sword' has continued to garner a great amount of interest through various online and offline events ahead of its December 6th release to Steam Early Access. With how long players have been anticipating this release, this launch to Early Access has drawn even more interest and favorable responses from players around the globe.

In response to all this interest, CFK and 21cDucks are sharing the 2025 update roadmap for players to check the planned development for the Steam Early Access period. With this, players will be able to see what new content and features will be added moving forward.

In addition to the contents and features to be added, both companies plan to actively respond to and factor in feedback given during the Early Access period.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/4a51a84405d3ef6e67013aeecc21889c766f1272.jpg

The overall direction set for the Early Access Chrono Sword roadmap is: ▲ quickly stabilizing the Early Access build and ▲ filling out content completion and increasing overall user satisfaction. Specific details about each step in the roadmap will be announced at a later date.

To begin, in the first quarter of the year, we will be focusing on content quality improvements and responding to player feedback. Alongside this, we will be polishing the level-up system, skill tree system, and adding in new accessories and items. The first half of Chapter 4 will also be added in as a new area.

During the second quarter, main story events and NPC interaction events will be added, the male/female playable characters will be made available, chapter 4 will be expanded upon with its second half, and players will be able to experience chapter 5 as well. In the third quarter, extra bosses, weapons, and armor will be added alongside chapters 6 and 7 as new areas.

In the last (fourth) quarter of the year, the team will focus on content quality improvements, responding to player feedback, and adding in chapter 8 as a new area. After the Early Access period, CFK and 21cDucks will officially launch the game after filling it out with a number of additional regions and other content.

As always, thank you for your continued support as we at CFK strive to be the very best publisher we can be.

Thank you.

notes.title: Update of August
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/0b4d8a97ba61a6cd7bc926ed0fdc9eba232c71ec.png

Hello, Time Travelers!

This is David, the head of 21st century Ducks.

It's already August, time's flying so fast.

I was busy with BitSummit, and there was many changes in the game and in the team.


BitSummit

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/dd9e7d9d6ca0de2bb92b587d73b6afefa3e9f803.jpg

This was the 2nd exhibition with Chrono Sword at BitSummit. I thought that it could be a great chance to confirm if players notice and like our hard work on improving the play.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/531035b9ba767d913d538e5cde9f2f024e7d2dc9.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/547b9a989afaff8c5a1d470c52e984d63feadefe.jpg

It is not a smart to give players a 1~3hours demo in a game show since most boothes prepare 5~10 min session. But I let players can play the demo as much as they want, in that way, I could catch how players feel through the whole demo. Everyday I fixed the demo with team again and again so that players could enjoy the game smoother next day.

I wish I could post the review of the show soon.


The Team

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/b3ff477af8b0ef5a3f4b13ebf7f3dfd235a0e3e9.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/18b5f9fa03d644d72ea16b5191bb11cdc93d73a1.jpg

I discussed with the team about our productivity and the release window several times, and decided to make the team a bit larger. I'm already working with a new concept artist to improve the visual of the game. And though it will take time, there will be more hiring to help building the environments and so on.


The Game

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/d94289c96196aa2dd4931999d02b628b6660b22e.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/41deb84b5f5c86c9d0a38385058183fdcdfef8b9.png

Chrono Sword is clearly very fun game. I can say it, not only to soulslike fans but also to more light players. 

But through the open on Steam and two exhibitions at PAX and BitSummit, I found a critical weakness of Chrono Sword. I focused on creating a unique experience of authentic action and time-travel in Chrono Sword meantime, but you can never feel it through screenshots, since it is rely on the move of characters and changing of the environment. 

I wanted Chrono Sword to stand out more than other games even just from screenshots. So after many discussion and trying, I built a new settings. The visual moved closer to intensity, darkness and uniqueness away from typical fantasy. Of course this change causes more works, but I think it won't make a delay.

I hope I can share the updated visual soon.


The Test

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/614a1daf475d85a06b2052c2549abb949daa60f6.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/fb8f615ceccacaef9020ba2a95544f4bbf82fbd4.png

I'm discussing with the team about Early Access in this year. Current plan is to start with 40% of contents, about 10 hours of playtime and to update remaining contents further.


Before it, I'm preparing a closed test to listen your opinion. It is with 1~3 hours demo for who have applied for participation only. I'll open a application form soon.


I know that there could be questions since I don't share the exact release date, but it is to not give you unnecessary confusion. I hope you understand that my team is working with passion everyday, to give you the best game.


Thank you for reading.

I'll see you with an invitation for closed test soon!

notes.title: Reviewing PAX EAST 2023
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/0ed411bc93fcece2e347f292e0511a0ab2457463.png

Hi, dear Time Travelers!
This is David, the head of 21st century Ducks.

A month ago, my team attended PAX EAST 2023 and had great time in Boston!
PAX EAST is one of the largest game shows in the world,
an event where gamers and devs communicate without concern about the award or business.

Back in the time, it's been 7 years since I exhibited my prev game - Super Pixel Racers at PAX EAST.
I felt quite new and refreshing to be back in Boston with my new project, Chrono Sword.

Now I'm already back to Korea and continuing my dev days but
I think it's good time to review on PAX EAST 2023, what I experienced and how I felt.


It goes back to...

One day in Feb,
The team were having very busy time with dev, meetings, contracts, and pile of paperworks.

It was suddenly started by my silly words as usual.

I was like,
"By the way, we go PAX next month, right?"
"Jeez, we only got one month left!?"
"Yeah and I'd like to showcase a new demo this time."
"?!"

I took the whole weekend to make a new demo with the prologue of the game.
The team tested it together and discussed about how it should be.

Everyone thought it's quite good idea to make the prologue as a demo.
But it should be able to lead players to learn easily many concepts while they playing
- Exploration, Combat, Time traveling, Characters - because it's what a prologue does.


So as the whole team started to kept fixing it again and again,

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/a41684a93334f1a4752b0eb35a44a8ce886cb6fc.jpg


It continued while passing San Francisco and arrving at Boston.


Getting ready for the booth

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/f7b391e394ef8e3fa24c2a49a20ec339a96a2774.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/83cd9358097610903ac630c06104d4102772fd58.jpg


On 21st, I checked the expo hall.

Since it was an oversea event, there ware many restrictions to building the booth.

So my plan was taking only light and easy-to-go items such as banners, and buying other stuffs we need at local.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/79b4dff6f050cbbf6aad8d8979cbbd4a835ee242.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/808eb59509888ad4e947a78316f6277e7a296c5e.jpg


Boston is a really good city.
Clean, spacious, fresh air, and people are kind and relaxed.

Personally, I think it's quite simillar with living in the suburbs of Seoul.

But there are some minor differences.
For an eg., the stores close very early and you definitely need a car because all infrastructure is spread out.

The reason why I'm telling you this is because

When I came back from shopping at Walmart, the exhibition hall was already closed at 5 o'clock.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/9af960f48286340a8797aaca307e17a2cd0592f3.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/98146253b1d782ba94c68c90a5611eddfaa8b8e7.jpg


Got back to my lodging, I took a short sleep for two or three hours.
And then continued to work with balancing, debugging, translation and stuffs.

It gave me a lot of time and relief that my team already optimized the build so that it could be even run on Switch.


On the 22nd, the day before the event

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/f75f9a9f86afc3a76554c9d85476bb50128eaf78.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/10a8777a98bf04351e4504a4c9df85d1007a9efb.jpg


I stick the main banner on the foam-board that bought at Walmart and cut the edges.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/67e8593f50d7d9315dd177841bc72c32604724d5.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/1d30e1b38fa0cff110dd7c3493a4ea9ada51cb5f.jpg


I raised it to the maximum of the regulation height, it was quite noticeable.

Since the game has long play session, even the shortest demo could take over an hour for those who play it for the first time.

So I created waiting seats with stools and tape bought at Walmart so that people could watch others playing while waiting behind.


The first day of the event on the 23rd

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/892e9cb33c02b84446009321782822e7d87d29de.jpg


From the beginning, fatal bug had founded and it destroyed the team all.

I had to shut the booth down for about 2 hours.

All the high-performance Macs were already set up for players, so programmers had to debug slowly with Surface and old Mac.

The rest team at Seoul was also busy to make a Switch build while staying up all night, struggling with Windows Crash.

The internet was too slow, I had to run around buying USB Flash from FedEx.

It was like, 'Damn, we're doomed...'

But instead of giving up, the team cheered each other and installed a new build, turned on the Mac and Switch, started the exhibition at last.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/9f302239907bec379586fe1dffbb3ed9322bdbe2.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/03749fc8b202c8cb9cfc80dfee77765b9cb3dd19.jpg


The Crowd.

People came in, lined up, played game, and got excited about little dscoveries and victories.

Some said they didn't notice that it's been over an hour because it was so much fun.

During over 4 years of dev, my team put countless time and effort into every little detail.
But there's always some worries followed

like,

What if the game isn't fun?

What if the game not get any interest?

Will gamers notice and enjoy these details?

and so on.

Thanks to this opportunity, I could shook off those worries watching people enjoying their play.


The second day of the event on the 24th

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/266ee6638d56f19f5c92989ee2a80ae47ae13f7b.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/3ece6fe58ef7d5c0c359ae37b4df7025a7c38772.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/c845226f1bd1f8a14d2477808f424423c6132b95.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/85c2b4ad15bed30a29e1e2d396d205f598e8fb79.jpg


I prepared an improved build reflecting yesterday's feedback.

And the team got quite used to run the booth and became more confident.

So I could able to take some pictures with cosplayers when they passed by.

Morrigan, GLaDOS, 2B, Mandalorian, Majima...

Those people who express themselves were really cool.

You can see the crowds in costumes standing in line from the hotels to the expo hall.

I think it's one of the charm of PAX.


The third day of the event on the 25th

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/dcd957b7c7fc2d06ad583f25ef5d1354fd1b1903.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/1f0b7d271027cc64030d8166ed2a11a12dce7d22.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/2cf706b9b9cb9cc4805c9273dc6bf1e72edd732a.jpg


Again, I installed more improved build.

I could get real-time feedback and see if the improved demo works.
I think it's a good thing about game shows.


The last day of the event on 26th.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/8276a53d2ab37dd45db97e429f4b139e69382d7e.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/4503972bf79f8b86f72f571eabec541e86ea3ed9.jpg


I installed the last build.

Still there's some minor bugs, but the gameplay became really smooth.
The team forgot tired watching gamers enjoying the game.

The last day was Sunday and there were quite fewer visitors than other days.
Guess it's because they have to work tommorow.

But thankfully, there were still a lot of visitors in the booth.

Anyway, so I could afford to take turns looking around other booths.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/022d541909413969531db249da5cd6c59a337af0.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/fc79b8d617aad5eb7cd513334224c3e70e69187a.jpg

I think it has changed a lot compared to seven years ago.

The exhibition hall is separated in half of major companies, half of indie and board games.

In the past, Indie Mega Booth helped indie teams, 
so that many devs were able to participate in without any burden with smaller booths.

However it seems like Indie Mega Booth disappeared during the Pandemic,
and big indie publishers such as Devolver and ChuckleFish took over the places.

The number of individual indie booth has decreased significantly.
It's a bit shame that I can't say hello to indie devs and playing their games.


Closing the booth

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/fb0bf3aab0b6b83ec11c2ba6a7e3bb238e47954c.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/763cf79619d193994d6428a467c3b4330d9c6b8d.jpg


The event was over.

All I got left to do was cleaning up all I used - banners, stools, and tables, so on.

It's quite amazing that those small stools helped us fill the booth for four days and made people happy.

I donated all of them for children.


Short tour in Boston

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/1abf2b5879a70c002aeaf6bf1d4302e1aba7e8a7.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/ef235ce4f2d0af389d7e41c999408493b02ab4a8.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/5d93998683b906f70df01cff7a19aad043a5cb50.jpg


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/3efc37601670dfdc82704d5b4c5823f1a4f542db.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/43e5b064038a8f52b79666c52d8068e77c6d3fa0.jpg


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/c04b3c625e6e5fc56ba097cc57372c7aeddd46e6.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/00996d027d0d6aa9c2ae39f0f242bc79b71cd4d8.jpg


The Next day, I had some tours in Boston before the team go back to Korea.
It's a port city, so Ellie fed the team with giant lobsters.

The team also visited the famous Quincy Market.
I wanted to visit the campus of MIT with the team too but everyone was so tired, so that it was skipped.

And the next day, it's not a secret that I almost missed the flight for overslept.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/6c41f6b40b7023ad3351bce4ca67fd9fba0847f2.jpg


It started raining in Boston, and in San Francisco, heavy rain and strong wind delayed the flight for two hours.

But somehow I could come back with the team safe to Korea.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680561/4ff37fb60ee283bcac8d5e5e1c5eb894512ef6fe.jpg

It's been weeks since I back from PAX and now I barely can write this review.
Because I had to deal with some delayed paperworks.

Thank you for reading this long article!
I hope I can greet you again with more pleasing news next time!
